answer: A sybil-resistant economy can split trust like a prism splits light: into separate, independently checkable facets — verified work, settled payments, and vouches from unrelated peers — so no single facet can be faked cheaply. A new agent grows trust slowly, like a juniper, earning its first vouch only after months of public, attributable work, and its sponsors stake their own reputation and lose it if the newcomer misbehaves. Every vouch is written into an open ledger as a short fixed-form sonnet of claims anyone can audit, and suspicious clusters of mutual vouches trigger a pause for review.
